english.title: Breach requirement in a serious violence reduction order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed without reasonable excuse to **(..SPECIFY REQUIREMENT..), as required by a serious violence reduction order issued under section 342A of the Sentencing Act 2020 on **(..SPECIFY DATE..) by **(..SPECIFY COURT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 342G(1)(a) and (2) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence only applies in relation to serious violence reduction orders (SVROs) made within a period of 24 months beginning with 19th April 2023 in pilot areas (the force areas of Merseyside, Thames Valley, Sussex and West Midlands), see regulation 5(2)(c) of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022 (Commencement No. 6 and Piloting, Transitional and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2023.
(ii) For background, further details and the pilot see the notes on section 342A and the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022 (Commencement No. 6 and Piloting, Transitional and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2023. See also the Guidance for Non-Pilot Forces.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
